arabic text:
Shab ki taariki mei, namaaz-e-shab ke baad, mera mazloom imaam, dua maang rahaa hai,
mere maula tujhe waasta, is gharib ke, ashkon ka, sukuune dil ke liye kar, mujhe sakina ata
Allah, Allah, Allah, Allah
Namaze Shab mei koi baap maangta hai dua
Allah, Allah, Allah, Allah, Namaz-e-Shab mei koi baap maangta hai dua
english translation text:
In the darkness of night, after the night prayer, my oppressed Imam prays:
My Lord, for the sake of this stranger's tears, grant me Sakina as the peace of my heart
Allah, Allah, Allah, Allah
In the night prayer, a father asks in supplication
Allah, Allah, Allah, Allah—during the night prayer, a father asks in supplication

arabic text: Sukuune dil ke liye kar, mujhe sakina ata\nAllah, Allah, Allah, Allah, Namaze Shab mei koi baap maangta hai dua
english translation text: For the peace of my heart, grant me Sakina\nAllah, Allah, Allah, Allah—during the night prayer, a father asks in supplication

arabic text: Diya hai sabr to mujko, karaar bhi dede, mehek batul ki haider, ka pyaar bhi dede, mei\nbaagh baagh rahun who, mujhe kahen baba\nAllah, Allah, Allah, Allah,
english translation text: You have given me patience; now also give me comfort. Grant me a daughter with Batul's fragrance and Haider's love\nMay my heart blossom when she calls me Baba\nAllah, Allah, Allah, Allah

arabic text: Who mere sine pe soye, to dharkane khush ho, chale who ungli pakar kar, to aahaate\nkhush ho, who maang paani to haathon ko mei karun kuza
english translation text: May my heartbeat rejoice when she sleeps upon my chest; may her footsteps\nbring joy when she walks holding my finger; when she asks for water, may I make my hands a cup

arabic text: Ibadaton ka silaa tujse maangtaa hun mei, yehi to eik dua tujse maangta hun mei,\ncharaagh-e-khaimaa bhujaawun, to who ho misle diya
english translation text: I ask You for the reward of my worship; this alone is the prayer I ask of You:\nwhen I extinguish the lamp of the tent, may she herself shine like a lamp

arabic text: Sunaa hai beti janaaze ki hoti hai ronak, mujhe bhi chaahiye quraane, zindagi ka\nwaraq, mile janaaze ki rounak, baraaye karbobala\nAllah, Allah, Allah, Allah,
english translation text: I have heard that a daughter adorns her father's funeral; I too desire a page\nfrom the Qur'an of life, so that my funeral may be adorned in Karbala\nAllah, Allah, Allah, Allah

arabic text: Khuda ne sunli duaae, hussein ibne ali, mili who beti jo bilkul, shabihe zahra thi,\nsukuun mil gaya sheh ko, sakina naam rakha\nAllah, Allah, Allah, Allah,
english translation text: God accepted the prayer of Hussain, son of Ali, and granted him a daughter who was\nthe very likeness of Zahra; the King found peace and named her Sakina\nAllah, Allah, Allah, Allah

arabic text: Magar sukuun ye karbobala mei jaata rahaa, huwi yateem sakina bandha rasan me\ngala, hussein rote the ye kehte barsare neza\nAllah, Allah, Allah, Allah,
english translation text: But that peace was lost in Karbala; Sakina was orphaned and a rope was bound\naround her neck. Hussain wept from the spear-point, saying\nAllah, Allah, Allah, Allah

arabic text: Pase hussein sakina ne who sitam dekhe, tarap ke kehti thi bachi, padar ke laashe se,\nchupaalo khun bhare daaman mei mujko ai baba\nAllah, Allah, Allah, Allah,
english translation text: After Hussain, Sakina witnessed such oppression; the child cried at her father's body:\nHide me within your blood-soaked cloak, O Baba\nAllah, Allah, Allah, Allah

arabic text: Sare hussein se aayi sadaa sare maidaan, namaaz-e-shab ki dua ka asar sakina jaan,\nkarenga teri hifazat wo naam hai jiska\nAllah, Allah, Allah, Allah,
english translation text: From Hussain's head, a voice came across the battlefield: the answer to the prayer\nof the night prayer, dear Sakina, will protect you—its name is\nAllah, Allah, Allah, Allah

arabic text: "Rehan azmi" kehti thi karbala ki fazaa, hai baap beti ka ye imtehaan kaisa khuda, har\neik zulm pe dono ke lab pe hai ye sada
english translation text: "Rehan Azmi", the air of Karbala asked: O God, what kind of trial is this\nfor a father and daughter? At every cruelty, the same words remain upon both their lips
